title: HTTP Client
subtitle: Small HTTP requests, directly from DuckDB.
intro: Fetch HTTP resources or submit JSON and form bodies from a SQL expression. Responses arrive as a JSON envelope containing status, reason and body, ready to inspect or save in a local table.

reference.name: http_get(url)
reference.description: Fetch a response; a three-argument overload accepts maps.

reference.name: http_head(url)
reference.description: Request response metadata without downloading the body.

reference.name: http_post(url, headers, json)
reference.description: Send a JSON body; headers are MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR).

reference.name: http_post_form(url, headers, params)
reference.description: Send form fields supplied as a VARCHAR-to-VARCHAR map.

reference.name: response->>'status'
reference.description: Read the HTTP status; cast to INTEGER for comparisons.

reference.name: response->>'body'
reference.description: Extract the body string; cast to JSON when appropriate.

notes.title: Materialize responses
notes.body: Requests are synchronous and buffer the response. Save responses to a table before repeated analysis. Deduplicate input keys for enrichment: a function evaluation can trigger a network call, and SQL evaluation order is not a request scheduler.

notes.title: Inspect status before parsing
notes.body: A body can be HTML, plain text or JSON. Check status and expected content before casting it. Endpoint authentication, retries and rate limits belong in the surrounding workflow; do not assume an HTTP error is a successful API result.

examples.title: Fetch once, inspect locally
examples.caption: Requires network access. The example.com response is HTML, so keep body as text.

examples.title: POST a JSON document
examples.caption: Replace the URL with your POST endpoint and add required authentication headers.
examples.reason: Requires a configured HTTP endpoint and sends data to it.

examples.title: Decode a JSON response body
examples.caption: Offline envelope fixture; returns the text value 42.

assertions: SELECT CASE WHEN ((('{"body":"{\"count\":42}"}'::JSON->>'body')::JSON)->>'count') = '42' THEN true ELSE error('HTTP envelope decode failed') END;
